name: Cap-Ferrat and the Riviera
tagline: Three corniches, hilltop villages, and the sea at every turn.
distinctive: The Riviera between Nice and Monaco combines Belle Époque villas, hilltop villages full of art, and three corniche roads stacked one above the other along the coast.

image.alt: The bay of Villefranche-sur-Mer and Cap Ferrat on the French Riviera

moodNotes.sea: Swim from the rocks at Cap-Ferrat and lunch at a beach club.
moodNotes.drive: The Grande, Moyenne and Basse Corniches are some of Europe's classic coastal drives.
moodNotes.art: The Fondation Maeght, Matisse's chapel at Vence, and Villa Ephrussi's gardens.
moodNotes.weekend: Nice airport is close, so a long weekend is easy from much of Europe.
moodNotes.lifetime: A convertible on the corniche at golden hour is as good as it sounds.

seasonNote: May, June, September and October are ideal. Summer traffic is heavy, and some hotels close in winter.

arrival.transfer: Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat is roughly 30 minutes by road from Nice airport, traffic permitting.
arrival.groundNote: Collect the car at the airport. Drive early in the day in summer, before the traffic.

driving.note: The corniches between Nice and Menton are classic drives. Summer traffic is heavy, so go early, and park in the villages rather than trying to drive through them.

carWhy: A front-engined convertible is at home on the corniche: roof down, unhurried, with the sea on one side.

transfer.label: Driver for evenings
transfer.why: Keep a driver for dinners in Monaco or the hill villages, so no one has to choose water over wine.

stay.name: Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat
stay.why: A Belle Époque hotel in large gardens at the tip of the peninsula, with the corniches on one side and the sea on the other.

watchWhy: A refined sports watch whose strap changes easily, from bracelet on the boat to leather for dinner.
aromaWhy: Green fig and sunny mimosa, both at home on this coast, with a trace of salt.

days.title: The cap
days.text: Walk the coastal path around Cap-Ferrat, then visit the gardens of Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild in the afternoon.

days.title: The Grande Corniche
days.text: Drive via Èze to La Turbie in the morning, have a long lunch, and dine in Monaco with a driver.

days.title: Art in the hills
days.text: Visit Saint-Paul-de-Vence and the Fondation Maeght, then Matisse's Chapelle du Rosaire in Vence.

moreDays.title: Antibes
moreDays.text: See the Picasso Museum in the Château Grimaldi and walk the ramparts.

moreDays.title: Îles de Lérins
moreDays.text: Take a boat from Cannes to the quiet, pine-covered islands.
